scope: Complete independent source-corrected twenty-member reconstruction shared by two overlapping original intakes. Raw RNA folding, complete 55/8 features, shared autoencoder pretraining, all configured initial supervised steps, all configured supervised/pseudo-label refinement rounds, checkpoint restoration, reverse-averaged predictions, all-member clipping and external generic ordered summation are retained. Recovered source is inference-only; training is reconstructed from the winner writeup with caller-controlled populations, splits, weights, steps, noise, reversal and rollback policy. Original winning clustered blend, historical schedule and accuracy are unproven. Both originals retain separate immutable provenance but do not represent two distinct algorithms. The ordered sum is domain independent; dense-feature training can accept compatible non-RNA features within fixed 55/8/5 dimensions and pinned architectures. Folding and ensemble/training policy remain recipe-specific. Shared pretraining and teachers are transductive; no independent cross-validation accuracy is claimed. Automated Tier 3 candidate; Tier 1 human certification and Tier 2 qualification are not claimed.
limitations: Automated Tier 3 corrected reconstruction. Original identities and immutable histories are preserved. Tier 1 human certification and Tier 2 usage qualification are not claimed.

The DasLab reconstruction uses twenty TensorFlow models: five states each of GRU, LSTM, forward and wave heads sharing an autoencoder-pretrained graph base. This is not the original winning clustered final blend or the intake PyTorch/PyG parallel-branch description.

Recovered source is inference-only. Training is reconstructed from the primary winner writeup with caller-defined populations, cluster IDs, proximity factors, splits, step counts, uncertainty eligibility/noise draws, reversal flags, rollback tolerance/policy and standard-deviation convention. Historical optimization schedule, noise distribution and accuracy are not reproduced.

Raw supported sequences are folded by the exact reviewed macOS arm64 CONTRAfold-SE executable with separately licensed EternaFold coefficients, default MEA decoding and posterior cutoff 1e-10. No independent solver or historical competition-output parity is claimed.

Features retain 55 node and eight adjacency channels, including capped Manhattan distance propagation rather than general graph shortest paths. Strict sequence/structure/probability guards and per-record feature batching correct source boundary and batch failures.

All-member clipping corrects the source first-member exemption and order dependence. Predictions reverse-average each model and average clipped member outputs; teacher moments use unclipped outputs and caller-selected ddof.

Source weighted per-sample per-target RMSE semantics include masked positions in the denominator and an epsilon floor. Null denotes missing serialized targets; nonfinite observed values are rejected. Population and fold construction are caller responsibilities, not certified independent validation.

Shared autoencoder pretraining uses the full labeled feature population, including member validation features. Pseudo-label teachers share population information; this is transductive and must not be presented as independent cross-validation accuracy.

Initial supervised and pretraining step counts are explicit. Each refinement round performs one full supervised batch and one pseudo-label batch per member. Validation may roll back model weights only or model plus optimizer, as explicitly selected. Exceptions in a refinement section restore both; stochastic RNG and iterators are not rewound.

Checkpoint files are private temporary runtime state and are removed after population execution. Native checkpoints preserve model and Adam state, not complete stochastic replay, external input provenance or interrupted whole-population resumption.

The execution seed changes process-global random state. Use a dedicated worker process; concurrent RNG isolation is not certified. Full graph evidence uses synthetic inputs, one refinement round and random initial weights, with no competition predictor weights or real records.

Pinned dependency closure and actual imports are qualified on the provisioned macOS arm64 Python 3.13 worker with legacy Keras. Clean installation, unrelated installed packages, GPU/mixed precision, other operating systems and resource limits are not qualified.
DasLab MIT and folding software/parameter licenses are retained. The linked notebook has no established reuse license and is comparison evidence only; its code is not embedded in this implementation.
The two intake identities describe the same solution family and share the exact same six providers. They are not independent algorithms or separate replication evidence.

The registered ordered numeric sum is domain independent. Feature-level training can accept compatible caller-defined graph features within fixed 55/8/5 dimensions and pinned architectures; cross-domain predictive quality is unproven. RNA folding and ensemble/training policy remain recipe-specific.

Historical source probes are retained without claiming they were rerun. Current native implementation evidence supersedes the historical environment qualification; each stored original additionally requires full execution and fresh reference comparison.

semantics.validity_bounds: Require exact dense-feature dictionary fields; deep-copy inputs. All three feature populations must be finite float32 node arrays (B,L+2,55) and aligned adjacency (B,L+2,L+2,8), with B positive and L at least two. Labeled targets must be float32 (B,L,5), allow NaN masks but no infinity, and satisfy every split observation/positive-weight constraint. Require positive Python integer pretraining and initial supervised step counts, Python seed in [0,2**31), supported rollback policy, finite nonnegative tolerance and Python integer ddof 0 or 1. Every round requires all twenty explicit member recipes with boolean reversal/eligibility arrays, finite float32 perturbations and nonnegative positive-sum float32 pseudo weights, at least one eligible positive-weight target and finite nonnegative uncertainty threshold. Use the hash-verified source architectures and legacy Keras. Reset the global TensorFlow/Python/NumPy initialization seed, so use a dedicated process rather than concurrent seeded executions. Preserve full model widths, caller step counts, all twenty members in sorted initial order and every refinement round. Shared pretraining uses the full labeled feature population, including validation features; teachers share member information, so validation is transductive. Each refinement round uses unchanged checkpoint teacher statistics, supervised training, pseudo-label training and configured validation rollback. Keep checkpoint weights and optimizer state in a private temporary directory; cleanup follows final inference. Load every final member with its manifest/family checks; predict forward and reversed inputs, average in native float32, compute unclipped float64 Welford moments, clip each member to [-.5,6] and retain the twenty-member stack. Model execution is serial; deployment must bound native/TensorFlow thread pools within the shared CPU budget. No raw RNA input or folding call is required by this operation.
